QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_5

question.text: An investor in Kaveri Macro Fund has NAV INR 120 per unit with HWM at INR 115. She redeems 40% of her units. After redemption, what is the HWM applied to her remaining 60% units for next-period performance-fee crystallisation?

answer.text: Remains at INR 115 (partial redemption does not reset HWM on retained units)
Weighted average of INR 115 and INR 120 based on redemption ratio

explanation.text: The Logic: A partial redemption crystallises performance fee on the REDEEMED units (fee charged on 120 - 115 = 5 per redeemed unit) but does NOT reset the HWM on the units the investor continues to hold. The retained 60% units carry forward HWM = 115. Next crystallisation uses that HWM vs fresh NAV. The Trap: Option A is the trap — students assume any fee-crystallisation event resets HWM (it does for the redeemed slice only). Option B confuses HWM with cost basis. Option D invents a weighted-average method that no PPM uses. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests HWM mechanics at the client level. XXI-B (Portfolio Managers) tests HWM for PMS. The no-reset-on-partial-redemption rule is consistent across Cat III PPMs and PMS fee agreements. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use a series-of-units (equalisation) approach rather than an investor-level HWM ledger — each subscription is its own series. On partial redemption, burn units in LIFO or FIFO per PPM; the remaining series retains its original HWM until it breaches again.
